headline: Discussed TPL ecosystem services proposal and NBCS native vegetation pilot project without taking formal action.
summary: The subcommittee discussed the TPL Ecosystem Services Proposal, noting that workflow 3 is no longer needed and that a civic assets study will exclude development potential on city parks and conserved open spaces. Dan Cahill reviewed a memo on the NBCS Pilot Project, and members discussed funding, project size, stewardship zones, and possible student involvement through Laura Hill's classes. No votes were recorded.

Open Space Subcommittee Meeting Minutes 
 
 
August 3, 2026 at 4:30 PM 
 
311 North Avenue, Conference Room or Remote via Zoom 
 
 
Present: Scott Gustin, Dan Cahill, Sarah Morgan, Zoe Richards, Rebecca Roman, Dale Azaria, Laura 
Hill, Michelle Lockhart, & Sharon Bushor.  
 
 
I. Public Comment 
Sharon Bushor was present and had comments for the full Conservation Board meeting.  She 
supports the TPL proposal.  She also spoke in support of the native vegetation pilot project.   
II. Discussion Items 
- TPL Ecosystem Services Proposal 
 
SG commented that workflow 3 in the proposal is no longer needed.  Sarah Morgan provided background 
relative to last week’s Planning Commission meeting and the decision to drop city parks from 
consideration for development potential.  The anticipated civic assets study will include all city lands, but 
part two of the study will exclude development potential on city parks and conserved open spaces.   
 
DA and RR asked for clarification. Sarah Morgan replied that there will be a study of all city-owned lands 
following adoption of PlanNNE to get a comprehensive understanding of those city assets.  Consideration 
of development potential will exclude city parkland and conserved open spaces.  SG noted next steps, 
follow up with TPL to drop workflow 3 and to bring the full Conservation Board an action item next 
month.  
  
 
- NBCS Pilot Project 
 
Dan Cahill overviewed the memo relative to the pilot project.  He’s looking to bring the full Board a more 
fleshed out proposal next month and the anticipated NOFO.  Items to consider include, but not are limited 
to, amount of available funding, project size, what are the goals?  Emphasize work within stewardship 
zones.
Sarah Morgan, outside of stewardship zones, perhaps consider proposals that could be a first step towards 
something larger in areas lacking stewardship zones like the ONE and Downtown.  Consider creative 
place-making, ecological and social significance.   
 
Michelle Lockhart, the BLUE program will have some sort of landscaping category that incorporates / 
emphasizes native vegetation for a stormwater credit.  The landscaping category would be new.  Any 
residential property can participate.   
 
Discussion about areas outside of stewardship zones ensued.  RR noted that as a pilot project, focus on 
stewardship zones is a solid approach.  It can expand and evolve over time.  Do we know what a given 
project should cost?  Dan, if we think through the lens of square footage and plants, we have good 
numbers.   
 
Laura Hill, my students can be resources for this work.  During the winter, plants are propagated in green 
houses from plants that were collected in the prior season.  Her students have helped with project 
planning.  ZR noted that the quality of work done by Laura’s students is very good.  Michelle, students 
could be involved with plant maintenance over time.  Laura Hill said that could be done, particularly over 
the summer, but that would require funding for interns.  During the school year, funding would not be 
needed. 
 
III. Adjournment 
 
5:28 PM.
